# AP-INC-002 Operational Incident Response and Review

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the procedures for the reporting, coordination, and review of all operational incidents occurring at AeroPolicy Airport. The purpose of this policy is to ensure a timely, consistent, and thorough response to incidents that may affect the safety, security, or efficiency of airport operations. It applies to all incidents that occur within the airside and landside areas of the airport, including but not limited to those involving baggage, restricted items, ramp safety, and equipment. The policy defines the roles and responsibilities of personnel involved in incident management and outlines the process for post-incident review to prevent recurrence and improve operational standards.

Operational incidents are defined as any occurrence that may result in or contribute to a risk to safety, security, or operational integrity. These incidents may involve equipment failure, human error, procedural non-compliance, or external factors. The scope of this policy includes the immediate response to the incident, the coordination of corrective actions, and the formal review process to identify root causes and implement preventive measures. All personnel are required to be familiar with and adhere to the procedures outlined in this policy to ensure a unified and effective incident management system.

## 2. Incident Categories

Incidents at AeroPolicy Airport are categorized into four main types: baggage, restricted-item, ramp safety, and equipment incidents. Baggage incidents include any event involving the misrouting, loss, damage, or delay of passenger luggage. Restricted-item incidents involve the discovery, handling, or improper placement of items that are prohibited or restricted by airport security regulations. Ramp safety incidents encompass any occurrence that compromises the safety of aircraft, personnel, or equipment on the ramp area. Equipment incidents refer to malfunctions, breakdowns, or failures of airport infrastructure, vehicles, or machinery that may impact operations.

Each incident category has specific procedures and escalation protocols that are detailed in related policies. Baggage incidents must be escalated in accordance with the procedures outlined in AP-BAG-001, specifically section 4, which outlines the required actions and timelines for reporting and resolution. Restricted-item incidents must be addressed in compliance with AP-SEC-003, which provides guidance on the handling and reporting of such items. The procedures for ramp safety and equipment incidents are integrated into this policy and are subject to the incident response and review process described in subsequent sections.

## 3. Reporting and First Response

All personnel are required to report any operational incident immediately upon discovery. The initial report should be made to the Reporting Staff Member, who is responsible for documenting the incident and initiating the first response. The Reporting Staff Member must ensure that the incident is accurately recorded, including the time, location, nature of the incident, and any immediate actions taken. This information is used to determine the appropriate level of response and to notify the Incident Coordinator.

The first response to an incident is the responsibility of the Reporting Staff Member and any on-site personnel involved. This includes securing the area, ensuring the safety of personnel and equipment, and taking any immediate corrective actions necessary to mitigate the impact of the incident. The Reporting Staff Member must also notify the Incident Coordinator within five minutes of the incident being reported, unless the incident is of a nature that requires immediate escalation to a higher authority.

## 4. Incident Coordinator Duties

The Incident Coordinator is responsible for overseeing the response to operational incidents and ensuring that all necessary actions are taken to address the incident and prevent recurrence. The Incident Coordinator must open an incident record for every reported incident before the end of the shift in which it was reported. This record must include all relevant details of the incident, including the time, location, nature of the incident, and any actions taken during the initial response.

The Incident Coordinator is also responsible for coordinating with the Airside Duty Manager and other relevant personnel to ensure that the incident is properly managed. This includes assigning responsibilities, monitoring the progress of corrective actions, and ensuring that all required documentation is completed. The Incident Coordinator must maintain communication with the Reporting Staff Member throughout the incident response process and provide updates to the Airside Duty Manager as needed.

## 5. Post-Incident Review

Following the resolution of an incident, a post-incident review must be conducted to determine the root cause and identify corrective actions. This review is led by the Incident Coordinator in collaboration with the Airside Duty Manager and any other relevant personnel. The review must include a detailed analysis of the incident, including the contributing factors, procedural lapses, and any equipment or system failures that may have contributed to the incident.

The review must result in a formal report that documents the cause of the incident, the actions taken to resolve it, and the recommended corrective measures to prevent recurrence. This report must be reviewed by the Airside Duty Manager and submitted to the relevant management for approval. The findings and recommendations from the review must be incorporated into the airport’s operational procedures and training programs to ensure continuous improvement in incident management.

## 6. Records

All incident records must be maintained in a centralized database and made available for review by authorized personnel. Each incident record must include the date and time of the incident, the location, a description of the incident, the names of the personnel involved, and the actions taken during the response and review process. The records must be retained for a minimum of two years and must be accessible for internal audits and regulatory inspections. The Incident Coordinator is responsible for ensuring that all records are properly documented, stored, and made available as required.
